summary: Week 6 pilot sync for Redwood Private VPC deployment. Main topics: routing/peering status, NAT and egress behavior, KMS access testing, and results from initial inference runs. Customer saw improved latency after kernel tweaks but reported intermittent 502s related to routing/NAT timeouts. Action items focus on network diagram, peering confirmation, additional benchmarks, and a security follow-up for SOC2/KMS integration.
transcript: Header: 2026-09-01 16:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Alex Chen, Maya Patel, Jordan Lee (Redwood) / Carlos Rivera, Priya Singh, Liam O'Connor, Nina Park (BlueWave)

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check - agenda for today is routing/peering, NAT/egress behavior, KMS access test results, and then bench results and next steps. Anything to add?
[00:14] Carlos Rivera: No, that's good. We mostly wanted to go over the 502 spikes we saw yesterday and confirm the network changes that Maya mentioned in the doc.

[00:28] Maya Patel: Yep. I put a note in the confluence - the short version is we recommended updating the route tables for the private subnets to point to the new peering attachment and adding a specific route for the inference nodes to use the NAT G W uh gateway in the transit subnet. Some of the transcribed notes said 'N A T gateway' which is fine, sorry for the bad auto naming from our last chat, but basically NAT vs direct internet egress is the lever here.

[00:50] Priya Singh: Quick sec, the security team flagged that KMS access from the cluster service account failed in one of our tests - the logs show AccessDenied for kms:Decrypt around 02:12 UTC. We wanted to confirm if the service principal used by Redwood is the one we gave in the IAM role or a separate managed role.
[01:12] Alex Chen: Good call. For the pilot we used a short-lived assumed role via our bootstrapper - that should map to the role you gave us. Maya, can you confirm the identity the runtime is using?

[01:26] Maya Patel: Yeah, we see the AssumeRole ARN in the agent logs - it matches the role listed in the onboarding doc but there was a timing window where the token refresh failed and the client retried which coincided with the KMS denial. I'm 80% sure that's the root cause, not a permissions misconfig. We'll attach the specific logs in the packet.

[01:52] Nina Park: We also noticed that when the retries happened, the egress path switched for a few seconds and that aligns with the 502s, so could be both token refresh and the transient route flop.

[02:10] Alex Chen: Ok, so two parallel workstreams: Maya to share logs and exact ARN usage; customer to confirm role mapping on their side. We'll also look at keeping a longer refresh window in the bootstrapper as a mitigation until we iron out the role chaining timing.

[02:34] Liam O'Connor: On routing: we accepted the peering attachment yesterday but haven't applied the route table change in staging yet. Wanted to confirm the exact CIDR you need us to route - earlier doc said 10.42.0.0/16, is that still right?

[02:50] Maya Patel: That's correct - the inference nodes are in 10.42.0.0/16. Also add a route for the health-checking subnets so our sidecar probes can reach the control plane endpoints. We should avoid 0.0.0.0/0 through peering, keep only the specific prefixes.
[03:12] Carlos Rivera: We're concerned about route table bloat. If we need to add multiple prefixes can we use a summarized route?

[03:22] Jordan Lee: Summarizing helps, but depends on your internal IP plan. We recommended a single /16 that covers the inference pool to avoid dozens of /24s. If you need more constraints, we can also support an NVA-style forwarding in the transit for more granular control.
[03:46] Priya Singh: Another security question - audit logs. We need proof of KMS key usage and Redwood's admin access to be logged to our SIEM. Does Redwood push logs or do we pull from CloudTrail?

[03:58] Alex Chen: For the Private deployment, audit logs are kept locally in your account - we can either forward CloudTrail to your SIEM or provide an S3 export snapshot daily. We'll include the exact CloudTrail configuration in the security packet. We'll also include example queries for key use, and the timeline of the test where the deny happened.
[04:18] Priya Singh: Please include the KMS key policy snippet - we need to show that the assumed role has decrypt/describe perms.
[04:28] Maya Patel: Noted, will include.
[04:34] [05:00] -- Benchmark results review -- Alex to present --

[05:00] Alex Chen: Alright, results. We ran the first 10k token benchmark on the pilot cluster using a quantized 7B model variant. Median p95 latency dropped from ~420ms to ~310ms after applying the kernel selection changes. Throughput improved by about 18%. Caveat: the small 502 spikes inflated p99 in one run.

[05:30] Carlos Rivera: That's promising, 310ms p95 is in line with our product target. The intermittent 502s are the blocker for us right now though - they're user facing if they happen during inference calls.

[05:46] Maya Patel: The 502s correspond to a proxy timeout - our sidecar returns 502 when the upstream connection drops during in-flight requests. We instrumented additional metrics and saw the egress connection to the control plane switching, likely due to route table re-eval or NAT gateway throttle.

[06:12] Nina Park: On NAT gateway throttle - we saw CloudWatch metrics spike around the same time. We do have some egress limits for unauthenticated flows. Can Redwood avoid outbound connections to public endpoints for model pulls? We'd prefer cached images in our private registry.

[06:28] Maya Patel: Yes we can configure image pulls from your private ECR and pre-warm the model cache. That should reduce public egress. For kernel updates we pulled a small patch from our update service; for the pilot we can stage those via your registry.

[06:50] Liam O'Connor: Good, that would remove a lot of the uncertainty. Also please confirm whether the runtime ever falls back to external hosted model endpoints - wanted to double-check we don't leak PII to hosted endpoints.

[07:05] Alex Chen: No fallback to hosted endpoints for Private pilot - the routing policy pins to local model artifacts. We documented the fallback policy but for this pilot everything is local-only unless explicitly toggled by a Redwood admin and with your approval.
[07:22] Priya Singh: Excellent. On to KMS: we attempted a decrypt test and saw the transient deny - we will send the CloudTrail snippet. Can you add a retry with exponential backoff for key ops?

[07:36] Maya Patel: Yes, the runtime already has basic retry but we can tune to backoff longer for KMS decrypt - that should reduce visible errors during rotations. We'll propose a small change and test it in staging.
[08:10] Carlos Rivera: Another thing - model quantization profile you recommended introduced slight quality regressions on our NER evals. Any quick tuning suggestions?

[08:24] Maya Patel: For NER we recommend mixing quantization profiles - keep the embedding and early attention layers in higher precision and quantize later layers. We also have a low-latency config that prioritizes p95 at a small cost to p50. We'll attach the profile diffs and the eval set comparison.
[08:46] Alex Chen: We'll include a small script you can run to reproduce the eval locally with our quantization suggestions, plus the exact seed so you get deterministic outputs.
[09:02] Nina Park: About upgrades - you pushed a kernel patch last week and we observed a small pod restart. Can you explain the rolling upgrade strategy?

[09:16] Maya Patel: Rolling upgrades are configured to do maxUnavailable 10% with health probes on start. The restart you saw was the kernel hotfix that required a probe to pass; we can reduce maxUnavailable further for production if you want zero disruption, but it will increase time to complete the upgrade.
[09:36] Liam O'Connor: We prefer slower upgrades for production. For the pilot, 10% is ok but will plan for 0% for canary in prod.
[09:46] Alex Chen: Noted. We'll document the canary params and the time window for patching. Also we'll provide a rollback step in the runbook.
[10:00] [10:10] -- Troubleshooting 502 sequence (reconstructed) --

[10:10] Maya Patel: Sequence we saw: token refresh fail -> client retries -> egress path transiently changes -> proxy sees broken upstream -> sidecar returns 502. Mitigations: extend token lifetime, tune KMS retries, route pinning to avoid transient path change, and pre-warm model cache to avoid extra egress during heavy churn.
[10:40] Carlos Rivera: That matches our observation. We'll prioritize the route table change and confirm when done. If that fixes it we can consider kernel tune a follow-up.

[11:00] Priya Singh: One more compliance item - can Redwood provide an encryption-at-rest architecture diagram that includes KMS key usage, key rotation cadence, and who has access to the key material?

[11:14] Alex Chen: Yes - we'll include a KMS flow diagram and the key rotation policy. Note: Redwood doesn't hold the key material for your pilot; keys live in your account and we only perform operations via the assumed role.
[11:30] [12:00] -- Next actions recap --

[12:00] Alex Chen: Recap: Maya will share updated network diagram, exact logs for KMS failure, and quantization eval diffs. Maya will also run the 50k token benchmark and post raw results. Carlos will validate peering and apply route table changes. Priya to send SOC2 scoping list. We'll schedule a security deep dive for next week. Anything else?
[12:34] Carlos Rivera: Add that we'll do a short hotfix window if the 502s persist after route change - we'll be ready to collaborate on timing.
[12:44] Alex Chen: Great - thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with the security packet and the benchmark uploads. Talk soon.
[12:55] Meeting end.
